HORA OS: 


SIXTY-THIRD ANNUAL REPORT 
OF THE BOARD OF 
DIRECTORS. 


Presented at the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Asssociation, 
May 2Ist, 1914. 


S we come to the close of another year we are profoundly 
grateful to God for what has been accomplished, and 
for many evidences of His help. The year has been 

one of steady growth in our Branches and of reaching out 
after new opportunities. 

We are glad to report that the Association is now estab- 
lished at seven different points in the city and district, and 
that, in addition, a far-reaching and highly efficient plan of 
work outside of the Buildings is in operation, under capable 
leadership. This advance over last year is due to the estab- 
lishment of a Branch in the east end of the city and the com- 
mencement of work for railroad men at St. Lambert. 

As our Branches have already held their Annual Meetings, 
at which reports of their activities have been presented, this 
report will seek to present those general aspects of the work 
for which the Board itself is responsible. Each of our 
Branches is in charge of a Board of Management elected from 
members of the Branch, who are immediately responsible for 
the local work. By means of monthly reports and by visita- 
tion the Directors have kept informed of their progress. Your 
Directors are glad to bear testimony to the efficient organi- 
zation of our Branches and the growing strength and experi- 
ence of our Boards of Management. We have great reason to 
be thankful for the raising up of new officers and committee- 
men who are so capable of carrying on this expanding work. 

That further extension will be necessary if we are to meet 
the rapid growth of the city, it is impossible to doubt. It is 
essential, however, that what has been so well begun should be 


5 


conserved and brought to the highest point of efficiency. Our 
greatly enlarged membership places a responsibility upon us 
‘tor intensive development at each point, and for the indi- 
vidual consideration of our members in order that the highest 
results may be secured. 

The membership of the Association has now reached the 
encouraging. total of 5,383, made up as follows: 


Men. Boys. 
Central: S45. 55. ce me cat sa ye arte aD Do 554

Last Year’s Recommendations —At the Annual Meeting 
last year several important recommendations were made for 
the coming year, and we are glad to say that each of these has 
received attention and progress made. Two may be mentioned 
here: 


1. The Library at the Central Building has received in 
special gifts and expended the sum of $400.00 for new books. 
The utmost use has been made of the funds available. The 
Library is in better physical condition and under better ad- 
ministration than ever before. It is rendering a unique ser- 
vice to.our membership and particularly to the thoughtful, 
ambitious class of young men in our midst. 

We suggest with great earnestness to our friends the pro- 
priety and usefulnes of special contributions towards the en- 
largement of the Library from the present 3,000 volumes to at 
least 10,000 volumes at the earliest possible time. 


2. The needs of the foreign speaking young men of our 
city have also received careful consideration by a special com- 
mittee. At our request Mr. W. W. Lee, Immigration Secre- 
tary at Quebec, spent several weeks in the city this winter 
making a careful study of the numbers, location, social, 
religious and economic conditions of this large group in our 
midst. His report has been referred to the Executive and 
Community Committees for final recommendations, and will 
be acted on at an early date. 


Point St. Charles Railroad Building—For several years 
your Directors have hoped that the work of this Branch might 


6 


be transferred from the present building to a new site, which 
would not only continue to serve the railroad men of that 
community but reach a larger number of the young men and 
boys of Point St. Charles. The matter was gone into carefully 
last fall but we are not yet able to report progress. 


Establishment of East End Branch—F¥or many years your 
Directors have had before them the needs of young men in the 
East End of the city—particularly the district adjoining 
Papineau and Delorimier Avenues, from Notre Dame Street 
north to the C. P. R. tracks. 

A eareful canvass of this district was made in 1912 by an 
energetic committee of young men in the Hast End, with the 
cordial support of their pastors, to ascertain the possible mem- 
bership there. 

After most careful consideration a vacant site was pur- 
chased in May on Papineau Avenue, facing Lafontaine Park, 
a little north of Sherbrooke Street. 

Pending the erection of a building, steps were taken to 
organize a representative Committee of Management and to 
formulate plans of work which might be carried on mean- 
while. Rented rooms were secured on November Ist, at 1333 
Papineau Avenue. With the assistance of the members, these 
were fitted up and furnished as a Social and Reading Room 
Centre, providing a headquarters for the activities of the 
Branch. The use of the Wm. Dawson School was kindly 
granted by the Protestant Board of School Commissioners for 
gymnasium clases and games. Up to date 149 members have 
enrolled and a very encouraging start made. 


Railroad Work at St. Lambert—The Grand Trunk Rail- 
way Company have recently opened a large new freight yard 
and terminal on their main line east of St. Lambert, which 
will transfer a large number of trainmen to that point. At 
the request of the officials of the company we are establishing 
a Railroad Branch there. A frame building has been altered 
and equipped by the company and an appropriation granted, 
which has made possible a commencement with Mr. N. W. ° 
Parker as Secretary. We trust that next year we may be able 
to present a full report of successful operations. 


Summer Camps—Our two attractive Summer Camps re- 
ported successful seasons. The Men’s Camp as Lake St. 
Joseph, in charge of Mr. H. C. Patterson, was open from July 
5th to September 2nd, with 160 men out. The Boys’ Cainp 


7 


at Lake Kanawana was open for July and August with 162 
boys, apart from visitors, in charge of Messrs. D. J. Evans, 
Harold Cross, and H. A. Lordly for successive portions of the 
season. The opportunity for healthful recreation and char- 
acter building which these Camps afford cannot be over- 
estimated. 


Highgate Conference—One of the most inspiring and 
helpful features of the year’s work was the second Conference 
at Highgate Springs, Vermont, when about one hundred of 
our members met over Victoria Day for conference about the 
Religious Work of the Association. Each Branch was well 
represented, and helpful suggestions gathered for the conduct 
of the year’s work. This conference will re-assemble again 
this year, on May 23rd, at the same place. 


Work in Foreign Lands.—For several years we have had 
our representative abroad in the person of Mr. C. S. Paterson, 
Secretary for Boys’ Work in Caleutta, India. We were 
pleased to have him home on furlough for several months last 
year, and to learn from his own lips of his work in the East. 
Our members and friends have raised a fund each year for 
the support of his work, and we are glad to note that the 
North Branch has united with the Central Branch in this 
undertaking. During the year $1,450.00 was remitted for 
this object. We trust that all the Branches will soon have a 
share in this unselfish task. 


Joint Current Expense Fund.—After ascertaining the sub- 
scription needs of the various Branches, the Finance Com- 
mittee, following the plan adopted two years ago, invited re- 
presentatives of the Branches to form a Joint Committee and 
conduct a canvass for the required amount. 


This was carried out during the last two weeks of October, 
particularly October 23-24 and October 31. The total amount 
of $20,819.50 was realized at that time. This effort was fol- 
lowed up by faithful work on the part of various committees, 
with the result that $28,293.16 has been received from this 
source, thus enabling the various Finance Committees to pre- 
sent a clean balance sheet at this meeting. 


We are greatly indebted to the generosity and public spirit 
of many of our members and subscribers who, by their gifts 
and in many eases by their active co-operation, have made this 
result possible. 


Community Committee.—It is impossible in the brief space 
of this report to fully describe the highly useful work of this 
committee, under the direction of Mr. Bradford. His services 
have been so varied and in such constant demand that he has 
rendered help at a great many points outside of his regular 
programme. This, however, has comprised the work of the 
Daily Vacation Bible Schools last summer; the evening use of 
the William Lunn School during the winter; Boys’ Club work 
in the city at large; the promotion of classes in English for 
foreign speaking young men; co-operation with other agencies, 
¢.g.. Sunday School Union, Young Women’s Christian Asso- 
ciation, Montreal Boys’ Club, University Settlement, ete, ; 
the training of leaders for Bible Class work, and lectures and 
talks on the general programme of Social Service. 


Staf.—In May last Mr. David Thomson, Secretary of the 
Railroad Branch at Point St. Charles, resigned to accept the 
Secretaryship of the Railroad Association at Kenora, Ontario. 
His place was filled by Mr. J. R. Mercer, of Allandale, On- 
tario, a former Assistant at Point St. Charles. 

Mr. J. G. McKay, Secretary of the Westmount Branch, 
resigned in May last to enter business, and his place was 
filled by Mr. J. Morley Carson, formerly Secretary of the Asso- 
ciation at Quebec. 

On June 1st, Mr. C. K. Calhoun entered upon his duties as 
General Secretary of the Association. Since that date Mr. D. 
A. Budge, our General Secretary for so many years, has acted 
as Consulting Secretary of the Association. 

Mr. John Bradford, of Amherst, N.S., entered upon his 
duties as Community Secretary, on July 4th last, bringing to 
our Association his unique experience in varied forms of ex- 
tension work. 

On April Ist, Mr. W. J. Green, Secretary of our Central 
Branch, tendered his resignation. His place“has not yet been 
filled. 

The Association has suffered a great loss this year in the 
death of our beloved Treasurer, the late Mr. L. H. Packard. 
For many years he faithfully served the Association, and, 
through it, the city of his adoption. | His place is hard to fill. 
We trust that his example and the memory of his achieve- 
ments will stimulate us all to greater zeal and more unselfish 
service for Jesus Christ. 

In elosing this report, the Directors would point out for 
the information of our members and friends that there is a 
mortgage of $60,000.00 on the Association Buildings, and a 


9 


floating indebtedness of $18,000.00 yet to be discharged, on 
account of the furnishings, which amount it was not possible 
to include at the time of the Building Campaign. We are 
also carrying a mortgage on the East End site. It is hoped 
that friends of the Association will bear these needs in mind 
and that funds may soon be forthcoming to discharge these 
obligations. 

The Directors wish to express the thanks of the Association 
to all who have in any way assisted in the work during the 
past year. Our thanks are specially due to the members of 
our Ladies’ Committees, to the city ministers for many acts of 
service, and to the daily press who are always so willing to aid 
the Association in its endeavors. 


Respectfully submitted, 


JOHN W. ROSS, President, 
C. K. CALHOUN, General Secretary.
